comments.author: @giannisolga5191
comments.text: I was expecting a deep dive into Edinburgh, Glasgow, Sir Walter Scott, tartans, regiments, Highland Games. This was more profound. I had heard of the Highland Clearances. But I had not acquired a great deal of knowledge about history back then. “That happened a long time ago,“ my interlocutor said.  Having studied the early Near Eastern civilisations, the 18th and 19th centuries feel very recent to me now. Close knit communities sharing common grazing lands feels right. Driving people off the land their family had farmed for centuries, against their will, is very cruel. One very distant patch in my patchwork family is Scottish. A Lowlands girl married a Highlander. He spoke Gaelic, which made him very exotic – not  considered a favorable asset.  Another, the same constellation, Lowlands girl and Highlander. He said he owned a croft. Everyone said oh yes knowingly and I was too embarassed to ask “What’s a croft?“ Thanks to you I now know. They sent me calendars of Scotland. Beautiful wild landscapes far away from civilisation and its discontents, making me yearn for solitude there. It is good to know the true story at a deeper level. Thank you.

replies.author: @WhereonEarth4K
replies.text: That's exactly the shift we hoped this could offer - the Clearances stop being a distant textbook line once you connect it to real families, even ones a few branches removed on your own tree. Glad "croft" finally has a face and a story behind it now instead of just a word on old calendars.
